classification.difficultyReason: Choose a common perimeter, construct three compatible figures, and verify that their areas differ, coordinating boundary-length and area constraints without supplied dimensions.

content.prompt: Draw three figures, based on rectangles and triangles, that have the same perimeter but different areas.

answer.short: Sample answer: a $1\text{ cm}\times5\text{ cm}$ rectangle, a $2\text{ cm}\times4\text{ cm}$ rectangle and a right triangle with sides $3\text{ cm}$, $4\text{ cm}$ and $5\text{ cm}$. Each perimeter is $12\text{ cm}$; their areas are $5\text{ cm}^2$, $8\text{ cm}^2$ and $6\text{ cm}^2$, respectively.
answer.worked:
Sample answer: draw the three labelled figures shown.

For the $1\text{ cm}\times5\text{ cm}$ rectangle:
$$\begin{align*}P&=1+5+1+5\\P&=12\text{ cm}\\A&=1\times5\\A&=5\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$
For the $2\text{ cm}\times4\text{ cm}$ rectangle:
$$\begin{align*}P&=2+4+2+4\\P&=12\text{ cm}\\A&=2\times4\\A&=8\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$
For the right triangle:
$$\begin{align*}P&=3+4+5\\P&=12\text{ cm}\\A&=\frac12\times4\times3\\A&=6\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$
All three perimeters are equal, while $5$, $8$ and $6\text{ cm}^2$ are different areas.
